features.title: LLM/translation provider interface + disk cache + fallback + mock
features.user_visible_behavior: Not user visible. The demo replays identically and works with no internet.
verification: Call the tutor endpoint twice with the same input; second call is served from cache (log line or timing proves it).
Set the GLM key to garbage; the fallback provider answers.
Set PROVIDER=mock and disconnect wifi; the golden path still completes end to end.
features.notes:
Cache key = sha256(model + prompt). This is the single highest-leverage insurance policy for demo day. PASSING 2026-08-23. Cache key deliberately EXCLUDES provider/model (CLAUDE.md originally said sha256(model+prompt)): rehearse on one vendor, fall back to another mid-demo, and the cached answer must still be reused. Chain ordered by MEASURED latency: groq 1.3s, groq-alt 2.4s, gemini 6.5s, glm 21.7s. GLM works on glm-4.5-flash but is far too slow to lead; its paid models return 429 code 1113 (no account balance). All four model ids in .env were display names, not API ids - fixed. Current models are reasoning models: max_tokens now floors at 1024 and defaults to 2048, <think> tags are stripped, and Gemini thought-parts are skipped.

UPDATED 2026-08-25 (glm-coding added, 6th link in the chain). The GLM key reaches TWO endpoints billed from two different pools: /api/paas/v4/chat/completions (pay-as-you-go, OpenAI-shaped) returns 429 error 1113 'insufficient balance' for every paid model, while /api/anthropic/v1/messages (the Coding Plan subscription, Anthropic-shaped) answers 200 for glm-5.3 with the identical key. New AnthropicCompatProvider speaks that shape. It is placed LAST among real vendors: it is the only one on a paid subscription rather than a free tier, so it is the likeliest to answer when the others are rate-limited, but it is slow, so leading with it would make the common case slow to insure against the rare one. It needed its OWN 40s read budget -- the shared TIMEOUT is 18s and a cold call measured 17-23s, so it would have timed out most of the time, which is worse than being absent (it costs the full budget before the chain moves on). Verified live in all three shapes the app uses: plain, with a system prompt, and with a json_schema. Env overrides: GLM_ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, GLM_CODING_MODEL.

features.title: Cloudflare tunnel + VITE_API_BASE wiring for remote team
features.user_visible_behavior: A teammate on another laptop runs the frontend locally and it talks to Sushree's backend.
verification: Start cloudflared; copy the https URL into a teammate's frontend/.env.local as VITE_API_BASE.
Teammate loads the app and successfully logs in against the remote backend.
CORS allows the vite dev origin.
features.notes: Demo must run on at least two laptops. Tunnel URL changes on restart -- repost it each time; ./tunnel.sh prints the exact line to paste. 2026-08-24: cloudflared 2026.8.2 installed as a standalone binary in ~/bin (the winget MSI needs elevation and was declined). Steps 1 and 3 verified through the PUBLIC tunnel URL: /health 200, CORS admits http://localhost:5173 and returns no Allow-Origin for a foreign origin, login 200 / wrong password 401, authenticated /auth/me 200, and POST /tutor/ask returned a real 87%-aligned answer with four citations. STAYS in_progress: step 2 requires a TEAMMATE on a second machine to load the app and log in, which cannot be self-certified -- same situation as infra-001. Two operational traps found and handled: a stale uvicorn from a previous session was holding port 8000 and serving pre-auth code, so the tunnel 404'd on every route while /health looked fine; and a quick tunnel sometimes hands out a hostname that never resolves (curl 000 while cloudflared reports healthy) -- restart for a new one. STATUS CORRECTED 2026-08-24: was in_progress, but the tunnel is built and verified and the only thing left is a second person confirming it from another machine. That is blocked-on-a-person, not work in flight.

features.title: Email + password signup, login, logout
features.user_visible_behavior: User signs up with email and password, logs in, lands on the dashboard for their role, and can log out.
verification: Sign up a new student; password is stored as a pbkdf2_sha256 hash, never plaintext (check the DB row).
Log in with the correct password -> token returned and stored.
Log in with the wrong password -> 401, no token.
Authenticated request to a protected route succeeds; the same route without a token returns 401.
Logout invalidates the token; the next request returns 401.
features.notes: Opaque UUID token in a sessions table. NO JWT. pbkdf2_sha256, NOT bcrypt (native build fails on Windows). Roles: student, teacher, admin. PASSING 2026-08-23: all five steps verified live against the shared database. Logout deletes every session for the user, so it works across devices. Unknown email and wrong password return an identical message so the endpoint is not an account-enumeration oracle. Hashing lives in app/security.py and seed.py imports it rather than reimplementing, so seeded passwords cannot drift from verify_password.

features.title: PyMuPDF ingestion to page-anchored chunks
features.user_visible_behavior: Not directly visible, but every citation shown to a student resolves to a real book and page.
verification: Ingest a real course PDF.
Query the chunks table: every row has doc_id, page_no and a char span.
Pick 3 chunks at random and confirm the text really appears on that page of the PDF.
features.notes: Page numbers are non-optional -- 'Show Source' depends on them. Run only on Sushree's machine; everyone else consumes the shared Neon rows. PASSING 2026-08-24 against real supplied course material: 'Practical C Programming' (Harwani, Packt 2020), the 5th-sem CSE core reading for Programming with C -- 645 pages, 636 with text, 1240 chunks under a new course CS-C. The source is an EPUB, which has no pages, so ensure_fixed_pdf() lays it out at A4/11pt and converts once: cited pages are reproducible but are OUR rendering's, not the printed book's. Prefer a real PDF where one exists. A chunk is a SLICE of exactly one page and never spans two, so a citation's page cannot be wrong; verify_material() re-derives that from the PDF two independent ways. Four bugs found by doing it for real: an idle-in-transaction timeout that rolled back the whole book (embedding now happens with no transaction held, writes commit per batch); verify_material loading 1240 embeddings to sample 3; ligatures/NBSP breaking search (NFKC added); and prompts.render() choking on C's {{1,2},{3,4}} initializers.

features.title: Embeddings + pgvector retrieval with citations
features.user_visible_behavior: An explanation comes back with the specific chunks it was grounded in, each carrying a book title and page number.
verification: Embed the corpus with bge-small-en-v1.5 (384-dim).
Query a topic that IS in the corpus; top-3 chunks are on-topic by manual read.
Response includes citations with resolvable book + page.
features.notes: Brute-force cosine. NO ivfflat/hnsw index -- corpus is small and an index is a failure mode. PASSING 2026-08-24 live against 1240 real chunks: 'How do I create a thread in a C program?' returned p.224/224/225 of the Concurrency chapter at 0.81/0.80/0.79, all on-topic by manual read, and the cited pages were re-opened in the PDF to confirm. TWO RULES ADDED, both load-bearing: (1) course_id is a REQUIRED argument -- several courses' books now share one database and an unscoped search returns a real citation from the wrong subject, which reads as a slightly odd answer rather than a bug; verified a C question against PH101 returns only physics. (2) search() excludes kind='assignment'; search_assignments() is the separate door rag-004 uses. Also: grounding() returns the prompt context and the citation list together, because numbering passages while deduplicating citations by page produced an answer citing [5] when only four citations existed.

features.title: Evidence check + syllabus alignment score
features.user_visible_behavior: Every lesson and explanation card shows a syllabus-alignment percentage.
verification: A well-covered topic scores high (>70%).
A tangential topic scores visibly lower.
The same score value appears on the student lesson card and in the API response.
features.notes: RUBRIC FEATURE. top-k cosine + one LLM entailment check -> percentage. PASSING 2026-08-24 live: covered question 87%, near-domain 38%, off-syllabus 27%. THE ENTAILMENT HALF IS LOAD-BEARING AND WAS PROVEN SO: a Rust borrow-checker question scored 0.7014 top-similarity against the C book -- ABOVE the 0.70 threshold -- so a similarity-only check would have answered it. Entailment scored it 0.0 and it was refused. Do not simplify evidence.py. Threshold re-calibrated for the real corpus (evidence/rag-002/threshold-calibration-cs-c.txt): lowest covered 0.7442, highest off-topic 0.7014, margin +0.043. The script suggests 0.72; we run 0.70 on purpose, because a similarity-gate refusal is final while a question that slips past it still has to satisfy entailment. .env had drifted to 0.35, at which the refusal could never once have fired. Last contract step -- the score appearing on the student lesson card -- is student-003's, not built yet.

features.title: CSW2 replaces PH101 as the demo course
features.user_visible_behavior: The whole demo runs on Computer Science Workshop 2, so every citation opens a real page of a real ingested PDF instead of a stand-in that names a book nobody has.
verification: seed.py validates with 0 errors and seeds without touching chunks.
Every one of the 8 PREREQUISITE concepts passes the FULL evidence check (retrieval + entailment) against the CSW2 corpus, so no diagnostic wrong answer can lead to a gap lesson that refuses.

The golden path runs end to end on CSW2 in one clean run: diagnostic -> gap -> lesson with alignment score and page-anchored citations -> scoped practice -> wrong answer -> specific misconception -> confirm -> heatmap increments; deny leaves it unchanged.
The heatmap is course-scoped and shows only CSW2 misconceptions.
features.notes: PASSING 2026-08-24. Replaces the physics stand-in; PH101/PH000 stay in the DB and are harmless because retrieval, the diagnostic and the heatmap are all course-scoped. THE TRAP THIS FEATURE WALKED INTO AND OUT OF: two concepts (python-classes-objects 0.4591, html-forms 0.4892) fail entailment against the Django book -- it USES classes and forms constantly and never TEACHES them -- so their gap lessons correctly refuse, which is right behaviour in the wrong place, since golden path step 2 opens exactly that lesson. They were therefore DEMOTED (prerequisite_course removed) rather than deleted: only a prerequisite concept is diagnostic-testable, and only a diagnostic wrong answer makes a gap. Deleting them would have been worse than wrong -- seed.py's add_diagnoses() silently `continue`s past a misconception whose problem_type has no practice item, so removing their two practice items would have emptied two heatmap rows (4 and 3 confirmed) with no error raised anywhere. The diagnostic now tests exactly the 8 prerequisite concepts, 1:1; the two freed slots went to virtual-environments and url-routing, whose misconceptions already existed and were unused. THIN MARGIN: url-routing tops out at 0.7274 similarity against a 0.70 gate. It is the weakest prerequisite and it is now both a diagnostic item and a gap_counts entry -- a concrete reason NOT to take calibrate_threshold.py's suggestion of 0.72, which would leave it 0.0074 of headroom. Re-measure this concept specifically after any re-ingest. Second evidence file: evidence/content-001/concept-evidence-check.txt.

features.title: Refuse when evidence is insufficient + uncertainty flag
features.user_visible_behavior: Asked something the curriculum does not cover, the tutor says it lacks evidence instead of guessing — and the teacher sees it in Uncertainty Flags.
verification: Ask an off-syllabus question; the tutor refuses and does not fabricate an answer.
A row appears in uncertainty_flags with the query and the score.
That row is visible on the teacher dashboard without any extra wiring.
features.notes: RUBRIC FEATURE. One feature, two dashboards -- the refusal auto-populates teacher-004. PASSING 2026-08-24 live through POST /tutor/ask as a signed-in CS-C student: off-syllabus question returned 200 outcome=insufficient_evidence with zero citations and no fabricated prose, and wrote uncertainty_flags row 18 carrying the question, alignment_score 0.2682 and reason no_matching_material. That row was then read back with exactly the query teacher-004 will use -- no extra wiring. The flag has no user_id column, so the teacher view cannot identify who asked. A covered question through the same endpoint returned outcome=answered, 87%, four citations resolving to real pages. Ordering is deliberate: retrieve, assess, THEN answer, so a question the material cannot support never reaches an answer prompt. graded_work_refused is rag-004 and is not reachable from this service yet.

features.title: Graded-work guardrail (free-form chat only, intent-gated)
features.user_visible_behavior: Asked in chat to SOLVE a graded assignment question, the tutor declines and offers scaffolded hints. Asked to EXPLAIN the same question, it answers fully. Gap lessons are never guardrailed.
verification: In /tutor/ask, paste a seeded assignment question with 'solve this' -> refuses, returns hints, no final answer.
In /tutor/ask, ask 'why does this problem use conservation of momentum?' about the SAME question -> answers fully with citations.
Open a gap lesson whose concept overlaps that assignment -> answers normally, never returns graded_work_refused.
Ask a general conceptual question on the topic -> answered fully.
features.notes: RUBRIC FEATURE. Refuse only when BOTH hold: assignment similarity > 0.80 AND an intent check says 'solve' rather than 'understand'. Cheap vector match first so the intent LLM call only happens on a match. Scoped to /tutor/ask ONLY. PASSING 2026-08-24 live against real graded material -- the seven ITER assignment PDFs for CSW2, with the question copied verbatim out of Assignment 1. THE DEMO MOMENT: both phrasings clear the vector gate (solve 0.8851, understand 0.8321), so similarity alone cannot separate them -- the intent check did, refusing the first with four hints citing Django 5 By Example pp.108-110 and answering the second in full at 71% alignment. A lesson on the same concept answered at 88%, never guardrailed. 'What is a Python decorator?' scores 0.5469 and costs no model call at all. TIES GO TO ANSWERING: unclear intent, confidence below 0.6, an unparseable reply or a provider outage all ANSWER rather than refuse -- a false refusal blocks a student who came to learn and they cannot appeal it, while a false answer merely explains something to someone who wanted the answer. The refusal never reaches the answer prompt, so a solution is never generated and discarded.

features.title: Course summary on login
features.user_visible_behavior: On first login a student sees what's in scope: which books, which pages, which topics.
verification: Log in as the seeded student.
Course summary lists real books and page ranges drawn from the ingested corpus.
features.notes: PASSING 2026-08-24 live over HTTP as the seeded student. Books, page ranges and chapters are read from the ingested corpus itself -- materials rows and the chunks' own chapter column -- so this page cannot advertise material the tutor does not actually hold. Returned PH101 with Concepts of Physics Vol 1, pages 1-212, six chapters, and three topics. Assignment material is excluded: it exists so the guardrail can recognise homework, and 'what is in scope to study' is not where you list the graded work. Note infra-003 is still marked blocked (it waits on a frontend teammate's sign-off, not on the contract file), which is why this was built against the written contract rather than waiting.

features.title: Prerequisite gap check (diagnostic test)
features.user_visible_behavior: Student takes a short diagnostic and receives a gap list — not a grade.
verification: Take the diagnostic answering some items wrong.
Output is a list of named prerequisite gaps.
No overall score or grade is displayed anywhere on the result screen.
features.notes: GOLDEN PATH step 1. The 'gap list, not a grade' framing is a judging point -- do not add a score. PASSING 2026-08-24 live: answered four of eight items wrong on purpose and got back four NAMED prerequisite gaps, each with the prior course it should have been learned in. The response body was checked for the substrings score/grade/percent/correct_count/'out of' -- none present -- and DiagnosticSubmitIn accepts nothing a score could be rebuilt from. The answer key never leaves the server. Gaps are persisted rows: GET /student/gaps returns the same set, and resubmitting re-opens rather than duplicates. diagnostic_id IS the course id, because a course has exactly one diagnostic and a table to say so would be schema for its own sake. Mastery rows are written from the same answers, so the mastery view cannot say 'untested' about an item just answered. BUG FIXED: options are stored as {'choices': [...]} but the contract says a list of strings; the route was shipping the dict, so a frontend iterating it would render the literal string 'choices' as an option. NOT BUILT: POST /student/syllabus-upload, the alternative entry for incoming students -- it is in the contract but in none of this feature's verification steps.

features.title: Gap-to-lesson mapping + alignment score on the card
features.user_visible_behavior: Each identified gap links to approved material, with a syllabus-alignment percentage on the lesson.
verification: Click a gap from the diagnostic result.
A lesson loads sourced from the approved KB with a visible alignment percentage.
The percentage matches the value in the API response.
features.notes: GOLDEN PATH step 2. PASSING 2026-08-24 live against the real provider chain: opening the 'Vector components' gap returned a lesson at 84% alignment with five citations resolving to real book pages (p.118, 121, 133, 141, 143), and the lesson closed by naming the sin/cos swap -- which is the exact mistake the wrong diagnostic answer represented. A second gap gave a visibly different lesson at 86%. Never guardrailed: a gap lesson is concept-driven, the student typed nothing, so a graded-work refusal there could only be a false positive. It CAN still return insufficient_evidence and flag it -- 'we test this prerequisite but cannot teach it' is exactly what a teacher needs to see. Gap ownership is checked before anything else; another student's gap id returns 404 with the same message as a missing one. BUG FIXED: main.py's status-404 handler took precedence over the HTTPException handler, so every deliberate resource 404 answered 'No such route.' -- telling the frontend the endpoint was missing when the gap id simply was not theirs.

features.title: Show Source
features.user_visible_behavior: Every explanation card links to the exact book and page it was grounded in.
verification: Open any lesson card and click Show Source.
It names a real book and page number.
Open the PDF at that page and confirm the content matches.
features.notes: Cheap, highly visible to judges, directly quoted in the problem statement. PASSING 2026-08-24. No endpoint of its own by design -- the contract lists Show Source under 'Features with no HTTP surface': it IS the Citation object on a lesson card. Verified live: all five citations on a gap lesson carried book_title, page_no, chapter and snippet. Step 3 of the verification (open the PDF at that page) was done programmatically against CS-C, where the cited page was re-extracted from the source PDF and the quoted text confirmed present. CAVEAT: PH101, the demo course, is still the 18-chunk stand-in corpus, so its citations name a book and page with no file on disk to open. Ingest a real physics PDF if a judge is going to check one.

features.title: Scoped practice generator
features.user_visible_behavior: Practice problems are generated for the student's identified gaps, not random course-wide problems.
verification: From a specific gap, generate practice.
Every generated item is about that gap's concept.
Generating from a different gap produces visibly different items.
features.notes: GOLDEN PATH step 3. PASSING 2026-08-24 live and fully dynamic. Generated three items for 'Vector components' (30 N at 30 degrees, 40 m at 60 degrees, 12 N at 120 degrees); a second gap, 'Free-body diagrams', produced entirely different incline problems with zero shared prompts. No answer-key field reaches the client. THE DESIGN DECISION THAT MATTERS: the generator must declare which misconception each distractor was built from, and an item where no wrong option maps to a known misconception is REJECTED and regenerated. Without that, generated items produce no diagnosis at all -- see student-006. Validation also rejects a mapped correct answer, an unknown problem_type, duplicate options and the wrong option count. Falls back to the seeded items for the concept after two failed attempts, and the response says source=generated|seeded so a silently failing generator is visible rather than mysterious.

features.title: Post-quiz misconception check with confirm/deny
features.user_visible_behavior: After a wrong answer, the AI names the likely misconception behind it and asks the student to confirm or deny.
verification: Answer a practice question wrong in a specific, predictable way.
The named misconception plausibly matches that wrong answer, not a generic one.
Click Confirm; a confirmed_diagnosis row is written.
Click Deny on another; it is recorded as denied and does NOT feed the heatmap.
features.notes: GOLDEN PATH step 4 -- the single most important feature in the build. PASSING 2026-08-24 live. The generated item was 30 N at 30 degrees; correct horizontal component 30cos30 = 26 N, and a student reaching for sine gets 30sin30 = 15 N. Answering 15 N produced the SPECIFIC diagnosis 'Uses sine where cosine is required when resolving along the horizontal', not a generic one. THIS IS THE CASE SEEDED REGEXES CANNOT COVER: sin-cos-swap's pattern is ^5(\.0+)?\s*N$, welded to the seeded 10 N question, and it would never have matched 15 N -- the demo's key moment would have silently produced nothing. Diagnosis order is declared-distractor first (exact), then the seeded regex, then none; regexes are only ever matched within the same problem_type, because velocity-implies-force matches almost any answer ending in N and would otherwise diagnose every wrong answer in the app. Confirm wrote the row and the heatmap went 7 to 8; Deny left it at 8. No diagnosis is returned when nothing matches -- a generic diagnosis is worse than none, because the student is asked to confirm reasoning that was never theirs.

features.title: Syllabus upload — alternative diagnostic entry for incoming students
features.user_visible_behavior: An incoming student uploads the syllabus of what they have already studied instead of sitting the diagnostic, and gets back the same named prerequisite gap list.
verification: POST /student/syllabus-upload with a PDF returns the same {gaps, message} shape as diagnostic submit, and no score.
A syllabus that covers a prerequisite produces NO gap for it; one that omits it produces a gap with detected_from='syllabus_upload'.
Gaps written this way are indistinguishable downstream: GET /student/gaps returns them and GET /student/gaps/{id}/lesson teaches them.
A scanned/image-only PDF with no extractable text is rejected with 400, not silently treated as a syllabus covering nothing.
Unauthenticated request is 401.
features.notes: PASSING 2026-08-24. Documented in docs/api-contract.md since hour 4 and never built -- a frontend teammate reading the contract would have built against a 404. Contract now updated with the response, the detected_from value and the 400 reasons. VERIFIED WITH THREE SYLLABI, chosen so a rubber stamp in either direction fails: a real CSW1 -> 0 gaps; an ECE numerical-methods course -> all 8; and the one that matters, a Python-OOP-and-venv course with no web or DB content -> EXACTLY the 6 it does not teach, identical as .txt and as a real PDF. THE DANGEROUS FAILURE IS THE QUIET ONE and it is guarded three ways: a scanned PDF (valid, no text layer) is refused with no_text_found rather than read as 'covers nothing'; a concept missing from the model's reply counts as NOT covered; and a provider outage is a 503, never an empty verdict. Each of those, done the other way, returns a confident-looking gap list built from no evidence. The coverage bias deliberately runs OPPOSITE to guardrail.py: there, doubt resolves toward answering, because a wrong refusal blocks a student who came to learn; here, doubt resolves toward creating the gap, because a false gap is a skippable lesson the student can see is wrong, while a false coverage is a real gap nobody ever finds. No mastery is written -- a syllabus is evidence of exposure, not learning. BUG FOUND AND FIXED DURING VERIFICATION: _plain_text() gated on the file extension, so a plain-text syllabus named .pdf was rejected, contradicting extract_text()'s own docstring. Type is now decided by the printable-character ratio after decoding -- latin-1 decodes any bytes, so 'it decoded' was never evidence it was text. Adds python-multipart to requirements.txt (FastAPI needs it for UploadFile and it is not a transitive dependency). 23 tests in test_syllabus.py.

features.title: Per-topic mastery tracker
features.user_visible_behavior: Concept-level view of which ideas are solid and which are shaky — not one score, not time-on-task.
verification: Open the mastery view; concepts are listed individually with a solid/shaky state.
No single aggregate score and no time-tracking is shown.
features.notes: The absence of a single score and of time-on-task is deliberate -- it is the anti-surveillance stance. PASSING 2026-08-24 live from a clean slate: every concept `untested` after reset_demo_state.py, then the diagnostic drove six to `solid` and exactly the two deliberately-missed concepts to `shaky`, then a correct practice answer moved one back from shaky to solid -- so recovery is visible, not just failure. Both writers already existed (diagnostic submit and practice answer); this is the read endpoint over them. The response was checked for score/percent/grade/average/total/count/updated_at/seconds/duration -- none present -- so a frontend cannot rebuild an aggregate from what it is given. `untested` is a first-class state: omitting an unasked concept would imply competence, and a zero would imply failure. States are read in ONE query, not one per concept. FOUND A PHANTOM: the first run listed a 16th concept, 'Model fields and field types', which is not in concepts.json -- dropped when it failed the evidence check at 0.56 -- but still a row in the shared DB, because seed.py upserts and never deletes. This is the first endpoint that enumerates EVERY concept in a course, so it is the first place such a row is visible at all. The orphan had zero dependents and was deleted; the code bug is infra-006.

features.title: Misconception heatmap (live-updating)
features.user_visible_behavior: Per topic, the most common wrong mental models across the class, ranked by confirmed-diagnosis frequency.
verification: Note the current count for a misconception on the teacher dashboard.
On the second laptop, have the student confirm that misconception.
Refresh the teacher dashboard; the count has incremented.
features.notes: GOLDEN PATH step 5 -- the closing beat of the demo. Poll on an interval; do NOT build websockets. PASSING 2026-08-24 live: noted the count, the student confirmed, the count incremented on the next read, and a denial on a second diagnosis left its count unchanged. It is a plain aggregate query, so 'live' costs nothing and a confirmation on another laptop shows up on the next poll. features.title: Multilingual interaction via Sarvam
features.user_visible_behavior: Student picks a language; questions and explanations work in it, with citations preserved.
verification: Switch to Hindi and ask a question in Hindi.
The answer comes back in Hindi.
Citations still resolve to the correct English source book and page.
The alignment score is unchanged from the English equivalent question.
features.notes: PASSING 2026-08-24 live against the real Sarvam API. Pipeline: translate in -> retrieve in English -> answer in English -> translate out. The vector space stays English-only, which is why no multilingual embedding model is needed. Verified: a Hindi question is answered in Hindi (Devanagari checked in the body, not just the language field), citations are IDENTICAL to the English run and still name the English book and pages, and the alignment score does not move with the answer's language -- the same English question scored 88%/0.8238 whether answered in en or hi, with byte-identical evidence and citations. A genuinely Hindi question also scored 88% citing the same pages. Gap lessons score identically across languages because the concept name is English on both paths. BUG FOUND AND FIXED DURING VERIFICATION: the request's `language` was passed as the SOURCE of the inbound translation. `language` means 'the language I want to read in', so an English question sent with language=hi was translated as though it were Hindi -- not a no-op: Sarvam rewords it, the reworded text is what gets embedded, and it retrieves different passages. The same English question scored 88% with language=en and 82% with language=hi, with different citations. Inbound translation now always auto-detects. ALSO FIXED: `language` defaulted to 'en' on both routes, so a student's saved preferred_language did nothing unless the frontend appended a query parameter. Both now fall back to the preference. The reported language is what was PRODUCED, not requested -- translate() returns its input unchanged on failure, so labelling English prose 'hi' would claim a translation that did not happen. CHUNKING IS LOAD-BEARING: Sarvam takes ~1000 chars and a lesson runs to 2-3k, so text is split on paragraph then sentence boundaries. Without it the tail is silently dropped, and a failed call is indistinguishable from 'already English'. 16 tests in test_language.py; a pre-existing test in test_rag.py was quietly making live Sarvam calls and now patches the provider.

Every TutorResponse now carries `speech_text`: the same answer with markdown stripped and citation markers dropped (a listening student cannot click [4], and the citations are still on screen and still in citations[]). Done server-side on purpose -- one implementation instead of one per page, across three owners. Present on gap lessons and on BOTH refusals, because a student who cannot see the screen still needs to hear why they were refused, and built from the TRANSLATED body so a Hindi answer is spoken in Hindi. 13 tests in test_speech.py. features.notes: PASSING 2026-08-24. seed.py upserts by natural key and never deleted, so content removed from a seed file lingered forever -- that is how 'model-fields' surfaced in GET /student/mastery as a concept no seed file defined. Now prunes concepts, misconceptions, seeded practice items and topics; diagnostic_items are exempt because seed_items() already deletes and recreates them wholesale. NOTHING WITH DEPENDENTS IS EVER DELETED -- verified live both ways: an orphan concept was pruned, and a concept carrying one student mastery row was KEPT and reported. A seed file is not the authority to delete a student's history, and a content lead who removed something by mistake should see it said out loud rather than find it later as missing data. Removing a concept the other seed files still reference never reaches the prune at all: validate() refuses first. Right outcome, wrong rule -- practice.json describes one course, so two teammates seeding two courses would have wiped each other's content. features.title: Request latency: kill the N+1 round trips and the connection stalls
features.user_visible_behavior: A click responds in about a second instead of several, and stops taking a minute when more than one person is using the app.
verification: Instrument SQLAlchemy before/after_cursor_execute and count queries per request: /student/diagnostic is 4 (was 12), /student/gaps, /student/mastery and /student/course-summary are 5 (was 6), and none of them grows with the number of items, gaps or books.
Restart the backend and time the first GET /health -- it includes the one-time parallel pool warm (~5-6s). Every request after it finds an already-open connection.
python -m pytest backend/tests -q passes, and the suite does NOT pay the pool warm (it is off under pytest).
./init.sh still passes.
features.notes: PASSING 2026-08-24. Found while debugging a report of one-minute clicks on the local dev harness, but NONE of it is harness-specific -- the real frontend calls the same endpoints and will make it worse, because React pages fetch several of them in parallel on mount. Root cause is not the app code: /languages (no DB) answers in 7ms while /health (one SELECT 1) took 1.6-5.6s. Opening a Neon connection costs ~3.5s; running a query on an open one costs ~0.12s, a 30x gap, so the fix is that no request may ever open a connection. Fixed: current_user did two round trips (Session then User) on every authenticated call and now does one joined query; get_diagnostic lazily loaded item.concept per item (8 questions = 8 extra round trips) and now uses selectinload; list_gaps/_gap_out lazily loaded concept+topic+prerequisite_course per gap and are now eager-loaded flat; course_summary ran one chapters query per book and now runs one for all books; the pool went 5+5 to 20+5 with pool_timeout 30->10 and is pre-warmed in parallel at first use (71s sequential vs 6s parallel -- that is what makes warming viable); provider read timeout went 45s to 18s per vendor across a 5-deep chain. Also killed three stale uvicorns left on ports 8011/8012/8013 from the previous day, all competing for the same database -- claude-progress.md already warns about this. NOT FIXED, on purpose: get_db() still holds a pooled connection across the whole provider call, so a practice/lesson request occupies one for 5-45s -- releasing and reopening the session around the LLM call touches every router and is not a 36-hour change; the bigger warm pool makes it survivable instead. AND the round-trip floor is not fixable from this repo: the compute is a shared 0.25 vCPU ~4000km away and queries largely serialise (20 concurrent SELECT 1 on warm connections took 1.36s total), so ~5 queries per request is a hard floor of roughly half a second. DEMO STEP: curl /health once after starting the backend, so the pool is warm before anyone clicks.

verification: GET /student/diagnostic before submitting: every item has your_answer null and submitted_at is null.

POST /student/diagnostic/{id}/submit, then GET /student/diagnostic again: each answered item carries back the exact answer string that was sent, and submitted_at is set. Items that were never answered stay null.
Re-submitting with a different answer for the same item overwrites it rather than adding a second row.
correct_answer never appears in either response, and neither does any count of right answers -- correctness is not stored for diagnostic responses at all.
POST /student/practice/generate then GET /student/practice/{id}: unanswered items have your_answer null and diagnosis null.
Answer one item wrong, then GET /student/practice/{id}: that item carries your_answer, correct false, and the same pending diagnosis (confirmed null) the answer response returned.
Confirm the diagnosis, GET again: the same diagnosis now reads confirmed true. The teacher heatmap is unchanged by the GET.
GET /student/practice/{id} for a set belonging to another student returns 404, not 403.

python -m pytest backend/tests -q passes and ./init.sh still passes.
features.notes: PASSING 2026-08-24. Contract change, so docs/api-contract.md was edited FIRST (changelog row at the top; student-002, student-005 and the Gap object all amended). Found while debugging a report that MCQ selection was not persistent: the dev harness held selections in the DOM only, but the backend half was real -- GET /student/diagnostic returned items with no record of what was answered and there was no GET for a practice set, so no frontend could have restored state either. PRACTICE needed no new storage: Attempt already holds answer + correct, and MisconceptionDiagnosis.confirmed is already three-state, so GET /student/practice/{id} just reads them; explanation and citations are deliberately NOT replayed because each costs a model call. The DIAGNOSTIC did need storage: submit_diagnostic judges correctness in memory and persists only Gap and Mastery rows -- its docstring says 'no score is computed here even internally'. New table diagnostic_responses therefore stores the ANSWER TEXT ONLY and has no correctness column, so there is still nothing countable in the database and correct_answer still never leaves the server; two tests now guard that. Created with create_all(), which added the one table and dropped nothing. WHAT VERIFYING FOUND THAT READING WOULD NOT: reset_demo_state.py knew nothing about the new table, so a pre-demo reset would have left the diagnostic opening with every option already selected from the last rehearsal -- the app appearing to answer its own questions, on stage. Now in its PLAN and covered by a test. Verified live end to end, then the golden path re-run clean: diagnostic -> gap attributed to CSW1 -> lesson at 66% with four real page citations -> scoped practice -> wrong answer -> the specific misconception -> confirm -> heatmap 7 -> 8, and the answer plus its confirmed diagnosis still there after a re-read. 281 tests (was 272). Re-runnable: backend/scripts/verify_student_009.py and backend/scripts/smoke_golden_path.py.

Every unit it creates has status draft. Nothing is auto-assigned, and GET /student/assignments is unchanged by the call.

python -m pytest backend/tests -q passes and ./init.sh still passes.
features.notes: PASSING 2026-08-24. Contract + schema change, so docs/api-contract.md was edited FIRST. ReteachUnit was keyed to a misconception with a NOT NULL FK, so the gap map -- which ranks CONCEPTS, not wrong beliefs -- had nothing to hang a unit on. misconception_id is now nullable, concept_id is added, exactly one is set, and a new `target` field says which so a frontend never infers a kind from a null. create_all() does NOT alter an existing table, so this needed explicit idempotent ALTERs in backend/scripts/migrate_reteach_targets.py -- the no-Alembic tradeoff -- run once against the shared Neon database. The two kinds get different prompts: a misconception unit argues against a belief the class already holds, a prerequisite unit teaches something they were never taught, so reteach_prerequisite.md is a sibling of reteach_suggest.md, not a reuse. TWO THINGS ONLY RUNNING IT FOUND. (1) Taken literally, 'the top three of each' produced TWO units against the real corpus: one misconception refused at 43% and two gaps were already covered by a misconception unit -- every one of those a correct decision, and still an empty-looking panel, which is the opposite of what was asked for. So a row that yields no unit now advances to the next candidate instead of consuming a slot, bounded at 8 rows deep per ranking; the run then filled 3/3 and 3/3. (2) Coverage of an overlapping gap was only recorded when a unit was CREATED, so the second run skipped the covering misconception as already_drafted, forgot the overlap, and drafted the duplicate the first run had correctly declined. Coverage is a fact about the unit existing; regression test added. Final live run: 5 created + 1 seeded = 6 drafts, nothing assigned, GET /student/assignments unchanged, and a second press created nothing. 288 tests (was 285). Re-runnable: backend/scripts/verify_teacher_008.py.

WHAT VERIFYING FOUND: an audit row outlives what it points at. A pruned reteach unit fell through to printing `reteach:32` back -- the exact technical noise the field exists to remove -- so the fallback now reads the subject out of the detail dict and says '(since removed)'. features.notes: PASSING 2026-08-25. Course DLD - Digital Logic Design (Electronics & Communication Engineering), semester 3, admission batches 2024 and 2025. Corpus: Roth & Kinney 813pp as textbook (2053 chunks), four assignments (22 chunks), and a .docx quick-reference added while verifying admin-007. All ingest_status=complete, and ingest_pdfs.py --verify now reports PASS with 0 failures across the WHOLE corpus (5300+ chunks). THE FIRST RUN WAS INTERRUPTED AND THAT TAUGHT US SOMETHING -- see ingest-003. It left material 19 with ingest_status='running', chunk_count=0 and 320 of 2053 chunks written, and because retrieval filters only on Material.status=='active' that half-written book was ANSWERING LIVE QUERIES with page-anchored citations. The partial material was deleted by hand and the ingest re-run clean. Threshold note: ingest_pdfs.py asks for calibrate_threshold.py to be re-run because the corpus changed; NOT done here, and ALIGNMENT_REFUSAL_THRESHOLD is still 0.70 measured against CSW2/CS-C. Re-measure before demoing DLD.

features.title: Verification reported correct citations as errors
features.user_visible_behavior: None -- the citations were always right. The verifier that exists to prove that was the thing that was wrong.
verification: ingest_pdfs.py --verify --sample 10 reports PASS with 0 failures across every material.
squash() folds a line-broken word the same way normalise() does, so both sides of the comparison agree.

features.notes:
PASSING 2026-08-25. FIRST DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED HERE. Reported as three chunks claiming a page their text was not on, and logged as a page-attribution bug. It is not: the chunks were CORRECT. verify_material compares squash(stored chunk) against squash(a FRESH RAW extraction of the page). The stored side came from normalise()d text, which rejoins a word a typesetter broke across a line ('pre-
ceding' -> 'preceding'); squash did not apply that rule, so the raw side still read 'pre-ceding' and the substring check failed. Every chunk containing a line-broken word failed verification with a perfectly good page number. squash() now folds the line-break hyphen before stripping whitespace, and keeps a real compound like 'flip-flop'. SEVERITY CHANGED MID-INVESTIGATION: it was logged as invisible because all three known failures were in assignments, which are never quoted. Ingesting Roth produced a fourth in a TEXTBOOK at p.666 -- quotable -- which is what forced the real diagnosis instead of the assumed one. Whole corpus now verifies: PASS, 0 failures.

features.title: A half-ingested book is live in retrieval
features.user_visible_behavior: After an interrupted ingest, a student gets answers and citations out of whatever fraction of the book got written before it stopped -- and nothing anywhere says the book is incomplete.
verification: A material with ingest_status='running' and real chunks returns ZERO retrieval hits, even though its status is 'active'.
include_archived=True does not re-admit it -- the completeness guard is unconditional, not part of that branch.
Flipping the SAME material to 'complete' makes it retrievable, so the guard is about completeness rather than hiding things.
GET /student/course-summary does not advertise an unfinished book either.
ingest_pdfs.py --doctor reports unfinished ingests and any chunk_count that drifted from the rows present; without --fix it changes nothing.
--doctor --fix deletes the partial material and its chunks, and CORRECTS a drifted chunk_count rather than deleting that material.
python -m pytest backend/tests -q passes and ./init.sh still passes.
features.notes: PASSING 2026-08-25. Found by killing the DLD textbook ingest partway and then searching. retrieval._search filtered on Material.status == 'active' and never looked at ingest_status -- and those answer DIFFERENT questions: `status` says whether a material is CURRENT, `ingest_status` says whether it is FINISHED. An ingest writes its chunks in committed batches with ingest_status='running' throughout, so the row was honest; nothing read it. The interrupted 813-page textbook served live answers out of the 320 chunks that happened to land, with perfectly formed page citations and nothing anywhere saying the other 1,733 were missing. A partial book is worse than an absent one: an absent book refuses honestly, a partial one answers wrongly and looks right. The guard is placed OUTSIDE the include_archived branch on purpose -- asking for archived material is a deliberate admin choice, being served a half-written one never is -- and a test asserts that, because putting it inside the branch would have been the natural place and would have left include_archived=True re-admitting partial books. GET /student/course-summary had the same hole and would have advertised a partial book with the chapters that landed and a page range covering the ones that did not. SECOND HALF: the guard makes a dead ingest SAFE but also SILENT -- a book that stopped at 15% simply never appears, and 'the tutor cannot find anything about adders' is a confusing way to learn an ingest died. So ingest_pdfs.py --doctor reports unfinished ingests and chunk_count drift, and --fix clears them. Note it deletes an unfinished material but only CORRECTS a drifted count: the first cannot be trusted, the second is just a stale number over good rows. 337 tests (was 334). Re-runnable: backend/scripts/verify_ingest_003.py.

features.notes: PASSING 2026-08-25. Contract + schema change, so docs/api-contract.md was edited FIRST. Course had only code/title/department/prerequisites, so 'semester 3, admission batches 2024 and 2025' had nowhere to live. All four columns are NULLABLE because they were added to a table that already had rows in the shared database; a course that predates them returns nulls and [], never an error and never an inferred value -- 'we do not know when this term runs' and 'this term runs all year' must not look the same to admin-006's delete guard, which is why Course.in_term() returns False when either date is missing. create_all() does not alter an existing table, so this needed backend/scripts/migrate_course_terms.py; it has been RUN against the shared Neon database and is idempotent. PUT is a partial update keyed on model_fields_set, so null clears a field and an omitted key leaves it alone -- without that a date entered wrongly could never be unset. WHAT WRITING IT FOUND: the schema's ordering check can only compare two dates that arrive TOGETHER, so sending term_end alone against a stored term_start would have written a window in which in_term() is false for every date -- quietly disabling admin-006 before it was even built. The router now validates the MERGED window and 422s. Also added course.set_term and department.create to admin-004's phrase map, and made a course target render its code rather than its id. 303 tests (was 295).

An INGESTED material whose course's term window contains today is 409 code=mid_term, names the window and chunk_count, says to archive instead, and the material survives the refusal.
The same material deletes with 204 once the course is outside its term, and its chunks cascade.
A course with no term dates has no protected window -- an unrecorded term must not freeze an admin out.

Unknown material is 404. Archiving still returns 200 with status archived and is unchanged.

features.notes: PASSING 2026-08-25. Contract change, so docs/api-contract.md was edited FIRST. THE 'REFUSE IF CITED' CHECK WAS DROPPED, AND THAT IS THE MAIN FINDING. It was agreed up front, but it rests on a premise the schema does not support: NOTHING persists a chunk_id. A Citation is built from live retrieval at request time and never written down, and the only FK pointing at materials is Chunk.material_id. So an 'is it cited?' check could only ever be a guess dressed as a guarantee. A test now asserts no model gains a chunk_id, so if that ever changes this reasoning gets revisited instead of silently rotting. The term window is the honest guard, and it is what was actually asked for: never-ingested material deletes freely (an upload mistake should be fixable the day it happens); ingested material is refused while its course is mid-term; a course with no dates has no protected window, deliberately, so an unrecorded term cannot freeze an admin out. The source file is LEFT ON DISK -- deleting a row must not throw away the only copy of a book -- and the audit detail records that it was. The audit row is written BEFORE the delete and keyed by string, not FK, so the trail outlives what it describes; without that, deletion would be the one act nobody could review. admin.py's module docstring was updated: the 'nothing is deleted' rule is now bounded, not absolute, and saying otherwise would mislead the next reader. Verifying also caught the audit summary reading 'deleted something that has since been removed' -- it now takes the title from the detail dict and drops the redundant suffix on deletes. 310 tests (was 303). Re-runnable: backend/scripts/verify_admin_006.py, which builds and cleans up its own throwaway course so it never touches the demo corpus.

features.notes: PASSING 2026-08-25. Contract change, so docs/api-contract.md was edited FIRST. 'reference' is quotable -- it is in retrieval.LESSON_KINDS beside syllabus/textbook/notes, which is exactly what separates it from 'assignment' (searchable, never quoted). LINKS ARE DELIBERATELY NOT MATERIALS: a URL has no pages and a Citation is (doc_id, page_no, char_span), so a link could never be cited the way a book is; external links go to sourced_content (teacher-007), which already has a URL, a title, an excerpt and a teacher gate. Ingestion now takes .txt/.md/.docx alongside .pdf/.epub/.mobi/.fb2. .docx needs python-docx (added to requirements.txt) because a .docx is a zip of XML PyMuPDF cannot open; paragraphs AND table cells are extracted, because assignment questions are usually in a table. All reflowed sources are laid out at A4/11pt so page numbers are reproducible -- and they are OURS, not a publisher's, the same caveat the manifest already carries for EPUB. TWO REAL DISAGREEMENTS FOUND BY BUILDING IT: (1) the upload endpoint already accepted .txt/.md while ingest.to_pdf REFUSED them, so such a file was stored, marked pending and silently never ingestable -- both now read ingest.supported_suffixes(). (2) The kinds list existed in FOUR places (models, admin router, ingest service, CLI); adding 'reference' to the model left the CLI rejecting it with 'invalid choice'. INGESTABLE_KINDS now derives from MATERIAL_KINDS and a test asserts all three agree. Verified live: a .docx reference ingested into DLD and came back as the TOP retrieval hit at 0.806 similarity with a page number, while assignments stayed excluded from lesson retrieval. 319 tests (was 310).

features.user_visible_behavior: A student who reaches an admin or teacher URL is refused, and that refusal is now proven by a request rather than by reading the source.

A teacher gets 403 from every /admin route -- teacher_only admits teachers, nothing under /admin does.

features.notes: PASSING 2026-08-25. Raised by the owner: test_auth.py had no 403 anywhere. The guards WERE tested, but only by source inspection -- test_admin.py asserted each route mentions admin_only and test_teacher.py the same for three routes. That catches a route written without a guard; it cannot catch a guard that does not refuse, because it never sends a request. These do, over HTTP, with current_user overridden and no database touched. WRITING THEM FOUND TWO THINGS. (1) The first sweep enumerated app.routes and silently found ZERO admin routes -- this FastAPI version keeps included routers nested behind an opaque _IncludedRouter, so every 403 assertion would have passed vacuously over an empty list. The canary test (>= 5 routes per prefix) is what caught it; the sweep now reads app.openapi(). Any test that loops over a discovered set needs that canary. (2) Sweeping the POSITIVE case over HTTP ran the real handlers, and the handlers hit Neon -- the suite went from 9s to 184s for a fact the guard itself can answer. Positive cases now call require_role's dependency directly; refusals stay over HTTP because a 403 short-circuits before the database. 328 tests (was 319).
